rules.statement: When the same derived result (such as merging layered settings) is needed in several places, compute it in one injectable service that every caller uses, not in hand-copied code or a static helper.
rules.why: Hand-made copies of the merge drifted apart: they read different sources and handled one scope differently. A static helper can't be replaced by a host and can't take the dependencies it needs.
rules.check: Look for new code that repeats an existing shared computation inline, or adds a static helper for logic that needs injected dependencies or that a host should be able to override.

rules.statement: Register a library's default implementation of a replaceable service with `TryAdd*` (for example `TryAddSingleton`), so an implementation the host registers first is kept.
rules.why: Hosts must be able to supply their own implementation, and every caller must then use the host's.
rules.check: Look for library service registrations that use `AddSingleton`/`AddScoped`/`AddTransient` for an extension-point interface where `TryAdd*` should be used.

rules.statement: Read `IOptions<T>.Value` when it is used, never in a constructor.
rules.why: Reading options in a constructor forces options validation, and every service that validation needs, to run while the service is being built, which can create construction-order problems and dependency cycles.
rules.check: Look for constructors that read `options.Value` or store it in a field, instead of keeping `IOptions<T>` and reading `.Value` in the method that needs it.

rules.statement: After a write, when code must see that write right away (seeding, previews, validation), read the committed state from the store, not a periodically refreshed or polled in-memory copy.
rules.why: A polled copy can be minutes behind the commit, even on the replica that made the change, so the follow-up work would miss the change or show stale state.
rules.check: Look for post-write logic that reads a cached or polled provider when it needs the value that was just committed.

rules.statement: Bulk read-only walks over many entities (for example a validation pass across all records) must read untracked, load only the fields they need with no secrets, and page with a keyset cursor ordered by identifier.
rules.why: Loading every entity with its secrets and with change tracking made a settings update unbounded and loaded sensitive data it didn't need.
rules.check: Look for loops over all tenants, clients or similar entities that load full tracked entities or secrets, or that load everything without keyset paging.

rules.statement: Run an expensive check that walks dependent entities after a change only when the change alters a value that the check reads; compare the effective values before and after the change.
rules.why: A change that touches nothing the check reads should load nothing, which keeps updates bounded.
rules.check: Look for update handlers that always run a full walk of dependent entities, without first checking whether any setting the walk reads actually changed.

rules.statement: A walk that spans tenants must run each tenant's queries under an explicit tenant scope, because tenant-filtered queries apply the ambient tenant's query filter.
rules.why: Without an explicit scope, the ambient tenant's filter would return the wrong tenant's rows, or none.
rules.check: Look for loops over tenants that query tenant-filtered stores without setting the tenant scope for each iteration.

rules.statement: When a stored settings document can't be read or honored, throw a `JsonException`-derived exception that names the scope and the owner of the document.
rules.why: Callers need to know which stored document can't be honored so they can report it (for example with a 409 response).
rules.check: Look for deserialization or merge failures of stored settings that are swallowed, or that throw a generic exception without naming the scope and owner.
